strategies.name: Naive sequential 8-stage all-reduce
strategies.desc: Implements the reference algorithm directly: 8 consecutive all-reduce dispatches, each preceded by a bidiagonal coupling loop and followed by an inverse coupling loop. Results in 8 all-reduce dispatches with full W*S payload each time. Maximizes readability and correctness verification but offers no optimization beyond the reference.

strategies.name: Fused coupling with vectorized operations
strategies.desc: Reduces local computation overhead by vectorizing the coupling/decoupling loops using torch tensor operations instead of explicit Python loops, but keeps 8 separate all-reduce dispatches. Same 8 dispatches as naive approach but potentially faster local computation through SIMD operations and reduced Python interpreter overhead.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduce-scatter + all-gather
strategies.desc: Replaces each all-reduce with reduce-scatter followed by all-gather to exploit potential intra-node bandwidth advantages. Each of 8 stages becomes 2 dispatches (16 total), but each dispatch handles smaller payloads (W*S/W = S per rank after scatter). Trades dispatch count for smaller per-dispatch data movement and potential parallelism.

strategies.name: Pipelined overlapping stages with buffers
strategies.desc: Allocates multiple buffers to overlap communication of stage i with local computation (coupling/decoupling) of stage i+1. Uses asynchronous all-reduce calls where available to hide latency. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but attempts to overlap their execution, trading memory (extra buffers) for potential wall-clock speedup.

strategies.name: Ring-based custom all-reduce per stage
strategies.desc:
Implements each all-reduce as an explicit ring algorithm using point-to-point send/recv operations, allowing fine-grained control over chunk sizes and pipelining within each stage. Increases total dispatches significantly (8 * W send/recv pairs ≈ 1792 ops) but exposes opportunities for micro-batching and custom bandwidth utilization patterns.
